data.name: Cyrano
data.gender_notes: Cyrano is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'kyros' meaning 'lord' or 'master', and 'anēr' meaning 'man'. In Christian tradition, Cyrano is known as a dedicated, romantic soldier, embodying love and loyalty. The name Cyrano carries the meaning “Soldier of love” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Cyrano usually hope their child will grow to embody soldier of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Cyrano represents the spiritual qualities of love, sacrifice, and selflessness. It is a name for those who are willing to put their hearts on the line for the ones they love, even if it means going against the odds.
data.etymology: Cyrano belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Soldier of love.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cyrano total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: In fiction, Cyrano de Bergerac is renowned for his eloquence, bravery, and tragic love story where he helps his friend Roxanne fall in love with him through letters, impacting the genre of romantic literature and the narrative structure of adaptations.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Cyrano epitomizes the virtues of faithfulness, self-sacrifice, and devotion, thereby inspiring a spiritual journey in its namesake. In a Christian context, Cyrano represents the sacrifice of Christ who gave up His divine power to inspired love on Earth, enabling humans to render their faith and loyalty unto Him.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cyrano de Bergerac, a legendary figure in Christian literature, represents the embodiment of noble spirit and selfless love. His large nose, a physical imperfection, symbolizes his inner depth and eloquence, transcending earthly vanity. His passionate devotion to Roxanne, despite his own insecurities, underscores the triumph of heart over appearance.

historical_references.reference: Cyrano de Bergerac was a French playwright, poet, and duelist. He was born in 1619 in Ronsard, France.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Cyrano remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Sarah Cyrano, a minister in Jerusalem, Israel, shares that their name Cyrano meaning "Soldier of love" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
